vendors.name: Daftra
vendors.tagline: Cloud accounting and business management for Arab-market firms, with Egyptian e-invoicing
vendors.market_position: Daftra is a cloud accounting and business-management system operated by Izam, Inc.; its about page says the company has headquarters in the United States and in Egypt. Daftra says 45K+ businesses use it and that it covers 50+ industries, with accounting, invoicing, inventory, CRM and HR modules. It runs Egyptian phone lines for 24/7 technical support and for sales.
pros: Vendor says it is fully integrated with the ETA e-invoice system at no extra fee
Accounting, invoicing, inventory, CRM and HR in one subscription
Published prices and a 14-day trial with no card required
Egyptian phone and WhatsApp lines for support and sales
cons: Priced in USD, so the EGP cost moves with the exchange rate
Lower plans cap monthly invoices, clients and warehouses
Extra users cost $7-9.33 a month each
ETA signing needs an e-signature certificate bought separately from Egypt Trust
vendors.typical_pricing: Basic $30/month, or $240/year ($20/month); Advanced $55/month, or $495/year ($41.25/month); Premium $70/month, or $600/year ($50/month); prices in USD as shown on daftra.com. Extra users $7-9.33/month each. 14-day free trial, no card required.
vendors.eg_specific_note: Daftra says it is fully integrated with the Egyptian Tax Authority's e-invoice system: it adds the ETA-required e-signature and digital stamp (the signature certificate comes from Egypt Trust), extracts GS1 item codes, calculates Egyptian VAT and can issue e-receipts. It says it charges no extra fee for the Tax Authority connection.

vendors.name: Edara ERP
vendors.tagline: Cloud ERP for Egyptian and Saudi trading and distribution SMEs, from Cairo-based Edrak Software
vendors.market_position: Edara is a cloud ERP from Edrak Software (EDRAK), which says it launched Edara in 2006 and lists an office in Nasr City, Cairo. It covers accounts, inventory, sales, purchases, manufacturing and point of sale, and the vendor aims it at small and medium trading and distribution companies in Egypt and Saudi Arabia.
pros: Published USD prices with monthly or annual billing
Accounts, inventory, sales, purchases and POS in one system
Vendor says it guides customers through Egyptian Tax Authority integration
Top plan connects to Shopify, WooCommerce, Salla and Jumia
cons: Egyptian e-invoicing is listed only in the top (Ultimate) plan
Priced in USD, so the EGP cost moves with the exchange rate
Every plan adds a monthly base fee on top of the per-user fee
Vendor aims it at trading and distribution firms rather than contractors
vendors.typical_pricing: Monthly base fee plus a per-user fee, in USD: Basic $29 + $5/user/month billed annually ($36 + $6 billed monthly); Professional $49 + $9/user ($61 + $11 monthly); Ultimate $79 + $12/user ($99 + $15 monthly). POS add-on $29/month. Egyptian e-invoicing is in Ultimate.
vendors.eg_specific_note: Edara says it shortens the steps to integrate with the Egyptian Tax Authority and follows up with the customer until the e-invoicing system is running; its pricing page lists Egyptian e-invoicing in the Ultimate plan. The vendor lists an office in Nasr City, Cairo, and Egyptian phone numbers.

vendors.name: AccFlex ERP
vendors.tagline: ERP and accounting programs with sector editions, including one for contractors
vendors.market_position: AccFlex sells ERP and accounting programs for companies in Egypt and Saudi Arabia, with sector editions for trade and distribution, manufacturing, ready-mix concrete, real-estate investment and construction, plus HR, cashier and sales-rep apps. Its construction program covers project management, construction contracts, payment certificates (مستخلصات), payment orders and cost allocation, the vendor says. The site is in Arabic and English.
pros: Dedicated construction and ready-mix concrete editions
Vendor says the construction program handles contracts, payment certificates and cost allocation
Vendor says it supports Egyptian and Saudi e-invoicing
Arabic and English site with a free accounting academy
cons: Only the small-business edition has a published price; the larger edition is quoted
Company location and history not confirmed in this check
E-invoice approval claim not checked against a regulator list
vendors.typical_pricing: Published by AccFlex: the startup and small-business edition (up to 10 users, core features, email support) starts from the equivalent of US$29; the edition for medium and large companies (all features, phone and remote support, users per contract) is priced by requirement.
vendors.eg_specific_note: AccFlex says its programs are approved by the Egyptian Tax Authority and Saudi ZATCA and support e-invoicing, and that its construction edition handles contractor payment certificates (مستخلصات). Ask for a demo of the Egyptian e-invoice submission before buying.

vendors.name: Wafeq
vendors.tagline: UAE-based cloud accounting with an Egypt site and EGP pricing
vendors.market_position: Wafeq is cloud accounting software from Wafeq FZ-LLC, a UAE company, with an Egypt storefront in Arabic and English and prices in EGP. It covers invoices, quotes, purchase orders, inventory, payroll and 40+ financial reports; Wafeq says more than 18,000 companies use it. Its documented e-invoicing is for Saudi Arabia's ZATCA; its Egypt pages make no claim about Egyptian Tax Authority e-invoicing.
pros: Published EGP prices for Egypt, monthly or yearly
Arabic and English interface
Invoicing, inventory, payroll and 40+ reports in one app
14-day free trial with no card required
cons: No Egyptian ETA e-invoicing claim on its Egypt pages
Contracts are with a UAE entity under Dubai (DIFC) courts
Support phone lines listed are in Dubai
Enterprise tier is quote-only and billed yearly
vendors.typical_pricing: Starter EGP 966/month, or EGP 805/month paid yearly (EGP 9,660); Plus EGP 1,386/month, or EGP 1,155/month paid yearly (EGP 13,860); Premium EGP 2,490/month, or EGP 1,991/month paid yearly (EGP 23,900); Enterprise on request, yearly only. No VAT note shown. 14-day free trial.
vendors.eg_specific_note: Wafeq has an Egypt site with Arabic and EGP pricing, but none of its Egypt pages, its sitemap or its developer e-invoicing guide mention the Egyptian Tax Authority; its documented e-invoicing is for Saudi ZATCA. An Egyptian business that must issue ETA e-invoices should confirm ETA support with Wafeq before buying.

vendors.name: DoubleClick ERP
vendors.tagline: Egyptian construction ERP linking the technical office to finance, with ETA submission of payment certificates
vendors.market_position: DoubleClick is an ERP from Click Enterprise, which says it has more than 20 years of experience, more than 3,000 clients and offices in Egypt and Saudi Arabia. Its construction edition connects the technical office (tenders, BOQ analysis, contracts, execution plans) to finance: owner and subcontractor payment certificates, site advances, equipment and fixed assets by project, with automatic ledger entries.
pros: Vendor says it sends payment certificates and invoices directly to the ETA
Owner and subcontractor payment certificates with deductions and approvals
BOQ items can carry unlimited cost elements and import from Excel
Tracks site advances and equipment by project
cons: No published prices; quote-request form only
No Egyptian street address on the site
Construction depth and ETA link should be tested in a demo
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices (the site has a request-for-quotation form).
vendors.eg_specific_note: DoubleClick says its program has a direct-link window to send payment certificates (مستخلصات) and invoices to the Egyptian Tax Authority, checks documents before sending, records the authority's validation afterwards, and prints the e-invoice QR code on the certificate.

vendors.name: Voko ERP
vendors.tagline: Cairo-built ERP with a contracting module and an Egyptian e-invoice module
vendors.market_position: Voko ERP is made by Business Force, a Cairo company (Nasr City) that says it was founded in 2007. Its contracting module covers projects, owner and subcontractor contracts, cost centres, BOQ and tenders (المقايسات والعطاءات), payment certificates (مستخلصات), site materials and purchasing, and the vendor lists AI-based budget forecasting. A separate module handles Egyptian Tax Authority e-invoicing.
pros: Construction module with contracts, BOQ, tenders and payment certificates
Separate Egyptian e-invoice module with e-signature and GS1/EGS coding
Cairo office (Nasr City)
Branch linking and permission levels
cons: No published prices; quote on request
AI forecasting and BI features are vendor claims to test in a demo
No free trial mentioned on the site
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices.
vendors.eg_specific_note: Voko says its systems automate the Egyptian Tax Authority e-invoice process: submitting invoices to the tax portal, signing them electronically and mapping items to GS1 or EGS codes, through its Egypt e-invoice module. The vendor is based in Nasr City, Cairo.

vendors.name: Namasoft (NamaERP)
vendors.tagline: Giza-based ERP with contracting, property and Egyptian e-invoicing modules
vendors.market_position: Nama ERP is made by Namasoft, founded in 2011 and headquartered in Mohandessin, Giza, with offices in Riyadh, Kuwait and Libya; the vendor says 700+ clients in 10 countries use it. Its 54 modules include financials, supply chain, HR and payroll, projects, and a property and contracting suite covering tenders, BOQs, payment certificates, retention and subcontractors. Named Egyptian contracting and real-estate clients include Nafal for Contracting, National Investment Company and Nablco.
pros: Contracting suite with tenders, BOQs, payment certificates and retention
Covers both ETA e-invoice and e-receipt systems, the vendor says
Head office in Giza with a Cairo phone line
Wide module range from finance to HR and payroll
cons: No published prices; demo and quote only
A broad configurable ERP, so setup takes implementation work
Construction depth should be tested in a demo
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices (the site offers demo booking).
vendors.eg_specific_note: Namasoft says Nama ERP covers both parts of Egypt's tax digitisation: B2B e-invoices with HSM signing and GS1 and EGS item codes, and electronic receipts for point of sale, submitted to and tracked with the Egyptian Tax Authority. It is headquartered in Giza and names Egyptian contractors among its clients.

vendors.name: Oracle Primavera P6
vendors.tagline: Oracle's project, program and portfolio scheduling system for large capital projects
vendors.market_position: Primavera P6 Enterprise Project Portfolio Management (P6 EPPM) is Oracle's system for prioritising, planning, managing and executing projects, programs and portfolios, which Oracle aims at asset-intensive industries. It runs on-premises or as an Oracle cloud service, and Oracle documents a current release, version 26. It is a planning and controls tool, not an accounting system.
pros: Plans and controls projects, programs and portfolios in one system
Runs on-premises or in Oracle's cloud
Actively developed: Oracle documents release 26
Oracle provides P6 training through Oracle MyLearn
cons: No price could be confirmed from Oracle in this check
Aimed at large, multi-project organisations rather than small contractors
No accounting or Egyptian e-invoicing; needs a separate ERP
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based through Oracle or its partners; no price could be read from Oracle's site in this check.
vendors.eg_specific_note: P6 plays no role in Egyptian tax or e-invoicing, so an Egyptian contractor needs a separate ERP for ETA compliance. Oracle's Egypt pages could not be read in this check, so local pricing, support and partners were not confirmed; ask Oracle or a local Oracle partner.

vendors.name: RIB Candy
vendors.tagline: Estimating, planning and project control for contractors, from takeoff to final certificate
vendors.market_position: RIB Candy is contractor software from RIB Software, which says it is part of Schneider Electric. It covers on-screen quantity takeoff, resource-based estimating, critical-path planning, cash flow, valuations, subcontract management and earned value, through to the final certificate. RIB publishes an Egyptian case study for Hassan Allam Construction and lists its Middle East office in Dubai.
pros: Takeoff, estimating, planning, cash flow and valuations in one tool
Egyptian reference: vendor case study with Hassan Allam Construction
14-day free trial
Desktop licences or a hosted Candy Cloud option
cons: No published prices; custom quote only
No Egyptian office listed; the regional office is in Dubai
An estimating and control tool, not accounting; no Egyptian e-invoicing mentioned
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. RIB says pricing depends on single-user or multi-user licences, with a Candy Cloud (desktop-as-a-service) option. 14-day free trial.
vendors.eg_specific_note: RIB's own site carries a RIB Candy case study for Hassan Allam Construction in Egypt, quoting its technical and tendering support senior manager on BOQ price matching and tender timelines, including work on the Benban Solar Park project. RIB lists no Egyptian office; its Middle East office is in Dubai.

vendors.name: Autodesk Construction Cloud (now Forma)
vendors.tagline: Autodesk's construction cloud, now Autodesk Forma: documents, model coordination, takeoff and project management
vendors.market_position: Autodesk Construction Cloud became part of Autodesk Forma on 24 March 2026, and its products were renamed (Autodesk Build is now Forma Build; Autodesk Docs is now Forma Data Management). Forma is sold in three bundles: Model Management (model coordination, design collaboration, Navisworks Manage), Preconstruction (takeoff, estimating, BuildingConnected bid management) and Construction Operations (Forma Build project management and submittals), each with Forma Data Management for documents.
pros: Model coordination and design collaboration in the Model Management bundle
Takeoff, estimating and bid management in the Preconstruction bundle
Shared document management across all bundles
User, project or account-based pricing options, Autodesk says
cons: No price shown on the pages that could be read; quote-based
Product names changed in March 2026, so older guides use ACC names
No accounting or Egyptian e-invoicing; needs a separate ERP
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; Autodesk's Forma pricing page shows no prices and says pricing can be per user, per project or per account. No list price could be read in this check.
vendors.eg_specific_note: Forma is a project and document platform with no Egyptian tax or e-invoicing role, so an Egyptian contractor still needs a local ERP for ETA compliance. Autodesk's regional and reseller pages could not be read in this check, so buy through an Autodesk-authorised reseller and confirm local support and pricing.

vendors.name: PlanRadar
vendors.tagline: Site task tracking, plans and documentation for construction and property teams
vendors.market_position: PlanRadar is a Vienna-based construction and property platform, founded in 2013, for site tickets and tasks on digital plans, checklists and reports, BIM models, document management and scheduling. PlanRadar says it has 200,000+ users in 75+ countries. Its Middle East office is in Dubai, and its careers page lists Cairo as a hiring location.
pros: Published per-user prices and a 30-day free trial with no card
Unlimited subcontractors and watchers on every plan
Arabic-language UAE website and a Dubai regional office
Pro plan adds BIM models, scheduling, approvals and API access
cons: A field and documentation tool, not accounting or cost control
Per-user pricing in USD adds up for large site teams
Plan and BIM-model limits per user below Enterprise
No Egyptian office listed on the contact page
vendors.typical_pricing: Basic $32, Starter $107, Pro $159 per user per month (USD, as shown on planradar.com; Basic is limited to 1 user); Enterprise custom. Annual billing saves more than 10%, and PlanRadar bills annually in advance unless agreed otherwise. 30-day free trial.
vendors.eg_specific_note: PlanRadar lists no Egyptian office on its contact page; its regional office is in Dubai, and its careers page lists Cairo as a hiring location. It has no Egyptian tax or e-invoicing role and prices are in USD, so EGP costs move with the exchange rate.

vendors.name: Odoo
vendors.tagline: Modular open-source ERP with an Egyptian e-invoicing localization
vendors.market_position: Odoo is a modular ERP whose apps cover accounting, inventory, project, sales and HR, sold as Odoo Online, Odoo.sh or on-premise. Its Egyptian localization includes an ETA e-invoicing module, available since Odoo 15.0, and Odoo's partner directory lists 204 implementation partners in Egypt.
pros: Egyptian e-invoicing module with ETA API, GS1/EGS codes and token signing
Accounting, inventory, project and HR apps in one system
Published prices, plus a free plan for a single app
204 listed implementation partners in Egypt
cons: ETA signing needs a USB token and Odoo's Windows IoT middleware
Construction workflows depend on apps and partner configuration
Total cost adds partner implementation to licences
List prices are in USD
vendors.typical_pricing: Standard US$8.95/user/month billed yearly or US$11.20 billed monthly (first 12 months discounted to $7.25 or $9.10 for initial users); Custom US$16.40 yearly or US$20.90 monthly (first year $13.40 or $16.90). One App Free: $0 for one app with unlimited users. Partner implementation is extra.
vendors.eg_specific_note: Odoo's Egypt localization connects to the Egyptian Tax Authority's e-invoicing API: the company registers its ERP on the ETA portal, maps products to GS1 or EGS codes, and signs invoices with a USB token from the ETA or Egypt Trust through Odoo's Windows IoT middleware. Odoo says Egyptian e-invoicing is available from Odoo 15.0, and its directory lists 204 partners in Egypt.

vendors.name: OrchidaTax
vendors.tagline: E-invoicing integration layer linking ERP, accounting and POS systems to Egypt's ETA
vendors.market_position: OrchidaTax sells an e-invoicing integration layer that connects existing ERP, accounting and POS systems to tax-authority portals, including Egypt's ETA, Saudi Arabia's ZATCA and the UAE FTA. It lists connectors for SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, Odoo, Xero, QuickBooks and Sage 50, and offices in Cairo, Dubai and Riyadh. It is a compliance bridge, not an accounting system; OrchidaTax says its parent, OrchidaSoft, was founded in 1997.
pros: Connects existing ERPs (SAP, Oracle, Dynamics, Odoo) to the ETA
Covers ETA e-invoices and e-receipts
Cairo office listed
Also covers ZATCA and UAE FTA for regional groups
Cloud or on-premises deployment offered
cons: Integration layer only; needs an ERP, accounting or POS system
No public prices
Little company background on its site
Sales-led: pricing only through a quote
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices on orchidatax.com.
vendors.eg_specific_note: OrchidaTax says it supports ETA Model 41 e-invoicing and e-receipts with digital signature, instant submission and submission monitoring, and lists a Cairo office in New Nozha. It suits a business that already runs SAP, Oracle, Dynamics or Odoo and needs ETA submission without replacing that system.

vendors.name: QuickBooks
vendors.tagline: Intuit's cloud accounting, sold in Egypt as the QuickBooks Global edition with no ETA link
vendors.market_position: QuickBooks Online is Intuit's cloud accounting software; outside its localised countries it is sold as a Global edition, and Egypt appears in the country list on Intuit's global site. Intuit's global pages list four plans (Simple Start, Essentials, Plus and Advanced, for 1 to 25 users) but say nothing about Egypt's ETA e-invoicing or e-receipts. It fits a business already on QuickBooks that will add a separate ETA connector.
pros: Familiar cloud accounting with a 30-day free trial
Multi-currency from the Essentials plan
Arabic-language version of Intuit's global site
ETA connectors such as OrchidaTax list QuickBooks integration
Intuit says you can switch plans or cancel with no cancellation fee
cons: No ETA e-invoicing described; a third-party connector is needed
Global prices load by location; no fixed figures on the page
Intuit says AI outputs are in English only
Intuit has closed QuickBooks in a market before (India, announced 2022)
vendors.typical_pricing: Four monthly plans (Simple Start, Essentials, Plus, Advanced) with a 30-day free trial; Intuit's global pricing page shows prices by visitor location, so check the Egypt price at quickbooks.intuit.com/global/pricing.
vendors.eg_specific_note: Egypt is in the country list of Intuit's QuickBooks Global site, but Intuit's global pages do not mention Egypt's ETA e-invoicing or e-receipt system. A business that must issue ETA documents needs a third-party connector; OrchidaTax, for example, lists QuickBooks Online and Desktop among its integrations.

vendors.name: Egypt Government Procurement Portal
vendors.tagline: Egypt's official government e-procurement portal for public tenders and auctions
vendors.market_position: Egypt's government e-procurement portal, described (in its own text quoted by TRACE) as managed by the Government Services Authority, an arm of the Ministry of Finance. Procurement departments publish tenders, auctions, evaluations and winning bids there, and accredited suppliers submit technical and financial offers online. It is the direct government source for public-works tenders rather than a commercial lead service.
pros: Official government source of tenders and auctions
Suppliers can submit technical and financial offers online
One accreditation covers all government entities on the portal
Publishes evaluations and winning bids
cons: Supplier registration and accreditation needed to bid
Site did not load for this check, so fees and features are unconfirmed
Tenders and awards only, not an early project pipeline
Ministry of Finance launched a new e-contracting system in 2023; its link to this portal is unconfirmed
vendors.typical_pricing: No fee schedule confirmed; check supplier registration terms on etenders.gov.eg.
vendors.eg_specific_note: For Egyptian public-sector work this is the government's own tender portal: procurement departments publish tenders and results there, and accredited suppliers bid online. Paid alert services such as EgyptTenders.com point to this portal, so compare any paid alert service against checking the portal directly.

vendors.name: EgyptTenders
vendors.tagline: Paid Egyptian tender alerts and contract-award data from Global Tenders Services
vendors.market_position: EgyptTenders.com is a paid tender-information service that says it is part of Global Tenders Services Pvt. Ltd. (GTS), a global procurement facilitator. It offers searchable Egyptian tenders from government departments, local authorities and private entities, daily email alerts and, on higher plans, contract-award data. It is an alert layer, not the official bidding portal.
pros: Published annual prices, from $295 USD
Daily email alerts and keyword search
Contract-award data on Premium and Platinum
Free sample tenders by email
cons: Official tenders are also on the government portal
Contract awards not included in Basic
Priced in USD
All sectors, not construction-specific
No operator address published on the site
vendors.typical_pricing: Basic $295 USD, Premium $395 USD, Platinum $495 USD, each for 12 months (1, 3 and 5 accounts); contract awards from Premium.
vendors.eg_specific_note: EgyptTenders emails daily Egyptian tender alerts and names the official etenders.gov.eg portal among Egypt's procurement channels. Weigh the $295-$495 yearly fee against checking the official portal yourself; the extra value is alerts, search and, on Premium and above, contract awards.

vendors.name: BNC Network
vendors.tagline: Regional construction project-intelligence database for the Middle East and Africa
vendors.market_position: BNC Network is a construction project-intelligence database that says it has operated since 2004 and covers 72 countries across the Middle East, Africa and South Asia. It sells project profiles with status updates, values, bidder information and contacts for owners, consultants, contractors and subcontractors. BNC describes itself as privately held and based in Sharjah, UAE, and an event sponsor profile names Industry Networks as its parent. The pages readable in this check do not name Egypt specifically.
pros: Project status, values and bidder information
Contacts for owners, consultants, contractors and subcontractors
Running since 2004 (BNC's statement)
Regional coverage for firms bidding across several markets
cons: Egypt coverage not named on the pages readable in this check
No public prices found
Site loads by script; little detail visible before contact
Regional database, not Egypt-specific
vendors.typical_pricing: No public prices found on bncnetwork.net.
vendors.eg_specific_note: BNC says it covers 72 countries across the Middle East, Africa and South Asia, but none of the pages readable in this check named Egypt or listed Egyptian projects. Ask BNC for a sample of its Egyptian project coverage before paying for a subscription.

vendors.name: MadeInEgypt
vendors.tagline: Free directory of Egyptian suppliers and brands, with a small construction-materials section
vendors.market_position: MadeInEgypt.com is a free directory of Egyptian B2B suppliers and retail brands; it claims 354+ B2B suppliers across 12 industries, and its construction category lists 21 companies covering cement, steel, glass, gypsum, tiles, waterproofing and marble. The site says browsing, contacting suppliers and listing a business are free, with no commissions. It is a supplier-discovery directory, not a source of project leads.
vendors.reputation_flag: The site labels its listings Verified, but its own disclaimer says it does not verify every listing and makes no warranties about the accuracy or legitimacy of listed companies. It names no operating company, and disputes go to binding arbitration in Orlando, Florida, USA.
pros: Free to browse, contact suppliers and list a business
Construction category covers cement, steel, glass, gypsum, tiles and marble
Site says no pay-to-rank and no commissions
Suppliers in 12 industries beyond construction
cons: Construction section is small (21 suppliers)
Disclaims verifying every listing despite Verified badges
No named operator or address
Mixes contractors with materials makers
Supplier discovery only, no project leads
vendors.typical_pricing: Free: browsing, contacting suppliers and listing a business (the site says no subscription fees or commissions).
vendors.eg_specific_note: A free starting list of Egyptian building-materials makers (cement, steel, glass, gypsum, tiles, marble), but check each supplier yourself: the site's own disclaimer says it does not verify every listing.

vendors.name: FilKhedma
vendors.tagline: Egyptian home-services app for AC, plumbing, electrical, carpentry and cleaning
vendors.market_position: FilKhedma is an app-based home-services company in Egypt offering AC maintenance, plumbing, electrical, carpentry, aluminium work, gas water heaters and cleaning, matched to its own 'FilKhedma Heroes'. Its site says it is 'A Shift South Company'; South Africa's SweepSouth, run by Shift South (Pty) Ltd, bought FilKhedma in December 2021, according to news reports. Its partners page lists Cairo, Alexandria and the North Coast.
pros: Covers core trades: AC, plumbing, electrical, carpentry
FilKhedma offers customers a 1-month quality guarantee
Partners page invites technicians to join
Part of South Africa's Shift South group
cons: Live areas limited to Cairo, Alexandria and North Coast
No public prices or partner pay terms
Terms and worker pages on its site show SweepSouth content
Residential home services, not commercial construction
vendors.typical_pricing: No public price list on filkhedma.com; bookings go through the FilKhedma app, and partner pay or commission terms are not published.
vendors.eg_specific_note: FilKhedma's partners page lists Cairo, Alexandria and the North Coast as live areas and invites technicians to become partners by email. Pay and commission terms are not published, so ask before signing up.

vendors.name: Misr Insurance Company
vendors.tagline: State-owned Egyptian general insurer, founded 1934, with a full engineering line
vendors.market_position: Misr Insurance was founded in 1934 by Talaat Harb and is owned through Misr Holding for Insurance, whose shares Presidential Decree No. 102 of 2023 moved in full to The Sovereign Fund of Egypt, according to the company. Al Chark Insurance and the Egyptian Reinsurance Company merged into it in 2007. It is supervised by the Financial Regulatory Authority under licence No. 1 and says its paid-up capital is EGP 8 billion.
pros: Engineering line covers CAR, EAR, contractors' plant and machinery, machinery breakdown
Owned via The Sovereign Fund of Egypt
Paid-up capital of EGP 8 billion (company figure)
FRA-supervised, licence No. 1
Hotline 19114 and branches in Egypt and abroad
cons: No published rates or online quote for engineering cover
Engineering page lists products, not limits or exclusions
No decennial liability listed on its engineering page
Branch count not published
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no published rates. Contact a branch or the 19114 hotline.
vendors.eg_specific_note: For contractors, Misr Insurance's engineering page lists contractors' all risks, erection all risks, contractors' plant and machinery, machinery breakdown and electronic equipment cover. It is FRA-supervised under licence No. 1, and the Egyptian Reinsurance Company merged into it in 2007.

vendors.name: Allianz Insurance Company Egypt
vendors.tagline: Allianz Group's Egyptian non-life insurer, with a published engineering cover range
vendors.market_position: Allianz Insurance Company - Egypt is the non-life arm of Allianz in Egypt, which says it began in 1976 as a shareholder in Arab International Insurance Company, raised its stake to 85% in 2000 and has traded as Allianz since 2004. It is licensed by the Financial Regulatory Authority (No. 2001/13) and lists engineering, liability, property, marine and motor cover for businesses. Its engineering page names five covers and says Allianz offers risk-management consultancy to clients.
pros: Engineering covers listed: CAR, EAR, plant and machinery, machinery breakdown, electronic equipment
Risk-management consultancy offered to clients
Serves construction, infrastructure, power and civil-engineering projects
Part of Allianz Group; in Egypt since 1976
Offices in 13 cities, from New Cairo to Luxor
cons: No published rates or online quote for engineering cover
Professional indemnity not listed on the engineering page
No decennial liability listed on the engineering page
Hotline open Sunday-Thursday, 9am-6pm only
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no published rates. Contact the 19909 hotline or info@allianz.com.eg.
vendors.eg_specific_note: Allianz Egypt's engineering page names five covers (CAR, EAR, contractors' plant and machinery, machinery breakdown and electronic equipment) and the sectors it serves, so you can see what is on offer before asking for a quote. Allianz Insurance Company - Egypt is FRA-licensed under No. 2001/13.

vendors.name: GIG Egypt (Gulf Insurance Group Egypt)
vendors.tagline: Gulf Insurance Group's Egyptian non-life insurer, with engineering and liability covers
vendors.market_position: GIG Egypt says it began insuring in July 1994 and is 99% owned by Gulf Insurance Group, a Kuwait-listed insurer in which Canada's Fairfax Financial raised its stake after KIPCO's exit in December 2023, according to news reports. Atlas Magazine reported in April 2023 that GIG acquired AIG Egypt. GIG Egypt holds FRA licence No. 9 of 1994, states issued capital of EGP 1 billion, and lists CAR, EAR, contractors' plant and machinery and electronic equipment cover.
pros: Engineering covers: CAR, EAR, contractors' plant and machinery, machinery, electronic equipment
Online engineering quote form and 19792 hotline
Professional indemnity for architects and engineers, plus public liability
99% owned by Gulf Insurance Group
cons: No published rates
No decennial liability listed on its product pages
Engineering page gives cover names, not limits or exclusions
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no published rates. Request an engineering quote online or call 19792.
vendors.eg_specific_note: GIG Egypt takes engineering quote requests online and lists professional indemnity for architects and engineers and public liability alongside CAR and EAR. Decennial liability is not listed on its product pages, so ask if your contract requires it.

vendors.name: Suez Canal Insurance (SCI)
vendors.tagline: Egyptian insurer founded in 1979 under Arab Contractors and the Suez Canal Authority
vendors.market_position: Suez Canal Insurance says it was founded in October 1979 as Egypt's first private-sector insurer, under the umbrella of Arab Contractors and the Suez Canal Authority. It holds FRA licence No. 5 of 1979, says it has 29 branches across all governorates, and lists engineering, fire, marine, motor, medical and accident cover.
pros: Engineering covers: CAR, EAR, civil works, contractors' plant, machinery breakdown, electronic equipment
29 branches across all governorates (company figure)
Founded in 1979 with Arab Contractors and the Suez Canal Authority
Online enquiry form for each product
cons: No published rates
No decennial liability listed on its engineering page
Current shareholders not stated on its site
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no published rates. Enquire through the product form on sci-egypt.com or a branch.
vendors.eg_specific_note: SCI's engineering page lists contractors' all risks, erection all risks, civil works cover, contractors' plant, machinery breakdown and electronic equipment, with an online enquiry form. Its links to Arab Contractors and the Suez Canal Authority date from its 1979 founding; the site does not state who owns it today.

vendors.name: Mohandes Insurance Company
vendors.tagline: EGX-listed Egyptian insurer with a full engineering line, from contractors' all risk to decennial liability
vendors.market_position: Mohandes Insurance Company is an Egyptian joint-stock insurer licensed in 1980 (licence No. 6) and listed on the Egyptian Exchange under the ticker MOIN. Its website names the Engineers' Syndicate pension fund as its largest shareholder (33.2%) and gives a paid-up capital of EGP 650 million. In February 2025 AM Best described it as a non-life insurer operating only in Egypt with about 3% of the market by gross written premiums.
pros: Engineering line covers contractors' all risk, erection all risk, contractors' plant and machinery, machinery breakdown and electronic equipment
Offers professional indemnity for engineers and decennial liability cover
Listed on the Egyptian Exchange, so its financial statements are public
Branches across Egypt, including Alexandria, Port Said, Suez, Mansoura and Assiut, plus the 19318 hotline
cons: No published premiums; every policy is quoted
AM Best noted a high reliance on reinsurance and a net book concentrated in motor
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public premiums. Mohandes takes quote requests and policy renewals through its website.
vendors.eg_specific_note: For contractors, the relevant covers on Mohandes's website are contractors' all risk, erection all risk, contractors' plant and machinery, professional indemnity for engineers and decennial liability for engineers' and contractors' civil liability. The head office is at 3 Midan Al-Mesaha, Dokki, Giza.

vendors.name: ZenHR
vendors.tagline: MENA cloud HR and payroll system with an Egypt payroll module in Arabic and English
vendors.market_position: ZenHR is a cloud HR and payroll platform that says it is localized for 11 MENA countries, including Egypt, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Jordan. Its about page mentions five offices across MENA, and its site lists contact numbers in Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Jordan. ZenHR names Vezeeta, Azza Fahmy and B-Tech among its Egyptian customers.
pros: ZenHR says its Egypt payroll automates income tax, social insurance, the Martyrs Tax and end-of-service gratuity
Handles social-insurance (ISTIMARA) forms, per ZenHR's Egypt page
Arabic and English interface
Pays salaries in EGP or USD
ZenHR states SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certification
cons: No public prices; a written quote from ZenHR sales depends on headcount, countries and bundle
No Egypt office or Egyptian phone number listed on its site
The Egypt page lists no income-tax rates or health-insurance handling, so confirm details in a demo
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. ZenHR says pricing is quoted per organization based on headcount, countries and bundle.
vendors.eg_specific_note: ZenHR's Egypt page says it automates payroll, income tax, social insurance contributions and ISTIMARA forms, the Martyrs Tax and end-of-service gratuity under Egypt's Labor Law, and can pay salaries in EGP or USD. It lists no Egypt office; its published contact numbers are in Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Jordan.

vendors.name: MenaITech (MenaPAY)
vendors.tagline: MENA HR and payroll suite with a New Cairo office and a free payroll plan for up to 30 employees
vendors.market_position: Menaitech sells HR and payroll software across the Middle East and North Africa, with MenaPAY as its payroll system and MenaSME as a cloud HR and payroll product for small and medium firms. Menaitech says its name has been associated with HR technology in the region for over 20 years. Its contact page lists offices in Riyadh, Jeddah, Amman, New Cairo, Dubai and Kuwait City.
pros: Office in New Cairo (5th Settlement) with an Egyptian phone line
Free Freemium payroll plan for up to 30 employees, in Arabic and English
MenaPAY handles retroactive calculations, provident funds and end-of-service settlements
Arabic Egypt site lists social insurance transactions in MenaPAY
cons: No public prices for MenaPAY, MenaSME or other paid products
Egypt pages give no detail on income tax, the Martyrs Fund or health insurance, so confirm the Egyptian setup in a demo
User and client counts on the site could not be read
vendors.typical_pricing: Freemium payroll plan free for up to 30 employees; MenaPAY, MenaSME and other products are quote-based with no public prices.
vendors.eg_specific_note: Menaitech has an Egypt website and an office in New Cairo (Azad Compound, 5th Settlement). Its Arabic Egypt pages list social insurance transactions and payroll in line with local law, but give no detail on Egyptian income tax or the Martyrs Fund, so check that configuration in a demo. Small firms can try the free plan for up to 30 employees.

vendors.name: Deel Local Payroll (formerly PaySpace)
vendors.tagline: Deel Local Payroll (formerly PaySpace): cloud payroll with Egyptian tax, social insurance and Martyr Fund rules
vendors.market_position: PaySpace, founded in South Africa in 2001, was bought by Deel in 2024 and is now sold as Deel Local Payroll, powered by PaySpace. The vendor says it serves 20,000+ customers and its countries page lists payroll rules for 49 countries, including Egypt. It suits employers who want in-country payroll in Egypt alongside other countries, either as software or as a managed service.
pros: Egypt coverage lists Employees' Tax, social security, Comprehensive Health Insurance and the Martyr Fund
Owned by Deel, with the same engine covering 49 countries
Per-employee, per-month subscription, with a fully managed outsourcing option
Payslips, leave and claims through WhatsApp self-service
cons: No public prices; cost varies by country, headcount and edition
No Egypt office; published contact numbers are in South Africa, the UK and Brazil
No Arabic interface mentioned on its site
No Egypt-specific product page, only a line on the countries list
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. The vendor charges per employee per month, with the rate varying by country, employee count and edition (Lite, Premier, Master).
vendors.eg_specific_note: Egypt is one of the countries on Deel Local Payroll's coverage list, with Employees' Tax, social security, Comprehensive Health Insurance and the Martyr Fund. The same engine runs payroll in the other covered countries, but the site lists no Egypt office or Arabic interface.

vendors.name: EgyBell
vendors.tagline: Egyptian outsourcing firm running payroll, social insurance files and HR administration as a service
vendors.market_position: EgyBell is an Egyptian outsourcing company that says it has provided HR outsourcing since 2015 and later added accounting and tax, procurement, legal and IT services. Its payroll service covers monthly payroll processing, salary reports, deductions and payment coordination, and a separate service handles social insurance files and labor office paperwork. It is a done-for-you service sold by consultation rather than self-serve software.
pros: Egyptian firm offering HR outsourcing since 2015, per EgyBell
Handles social insurance files and labor office documentation for you
One provider for payroll, recruitment, personnel archiving and accounting and tax
Reachable by phone or WhatsApp on an Egyptian number
cons: No public prices; every engagement starts with a consultation
No street address or named clients on its website
No published service levels
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. EgyBell prices each outsourcing engagement after a consultation.
vendors.eg_specific_note: EgyBell describes its services as covering Egypt and sells payroll as an outsourced service: its team processes monthly payroll and, under a separate service, handles social insurance files and labor office documentation. That suits a contractor who wants the paperwork handled rather than another system to run.

vendors.name: Egyptian Federation for Construction & Building Contractors (EFCBC)
vendors.tagline: Statutory federation every Egyptian contractor must join before taking contracting work above EGP 50,000
vendors.market_position: The Egyptian Federation for Construction and Building Contractors was set up by Law 104 of 1992. Under the law every person or company engaged in contracting is a working member, and no contracting work worth more than EGP 50,000 per operation may be assigned to or carried out by a non-member. The federation classifies and ranks its members by specialization and capacity.
pros: Membership is the legal condition for contracting work above EGP 50,000 per operation
Classification by specialization and capacity gives clients a recognized grade
Foreign contractors have a route in as corresponding members
The law provides an optional arbitration system for disputes between members and clients
cons: Contracting above EGP 50,000 without registration is punishable by a fine (EGP 1,000-10,000 in the 1992 text) and the contract is annulled
Hiring or assigning work to non-members is also an offence
Fees, class rules and document lists are not readable on the federation's website
The federation can discipline members, up to exclusion for up to a year
vendors.typical_pricing: Official fees: a one-off registration fee and an annual subscription set by the federation's executive regulations; current amounts are not published in readable form on its website.
vendors.eg_specific_note: Law 104/1992 (Art. 7) bars anyone who is not a working member from taking contracting work worth more than EGP 50,000 per operation, and Art. 46 makes the court annul such contracts and order compensation to the federation equal to the fees owed. Register before signing a contract above that value.

vendors.name: Egyptian Engineers Syndicate
vendors.tagline: Statutory engineers' syndicate: engineering posts and work in Egypt go only to registered engineers or permit holders
vendors.market_position: The Engineers Syndicate was established by Law 66 of 1974 as the body representing Egypt's engineers, with its headquarters in Cairo and branches in the governorates. Under Article 7, ministries, public bodies, companies and individuals may only appoint engineers or assign engineering works to engineers or consulting offices registered with the syndicate. Foreign engineers and foreign consulting offices need a specific practice permit requested by the entity that engaged them.
pros: Registration is the legal condition for engineering posts and engineering work in Egypt
Consulting engineering offices can also be registered
The law sets up a pensions and assistance fund for members
A route exists for foreign engineers through specific practice permits
cons: Every engineer registers individually and pays an annual subscription
Services are suspended if the annual subscription is not paid by 31 December
Practising without registration is a criminal offence under the law
Current fees could not be read on the syndicate's website
vendors.typical_pricing: Official fees: a registration fee and an annual subscription per engineer, plus permit fees for foreign engineers, set under Law 66 of 1974 and the syndicate's rules; current amounts are not published in readable form on its website.
vendors.eg_specific_note: A contractor may only give engineering posts and engineering work to engineers or consulting offices registered with the syndicate (Law 66/1974, Art. 7), so check each site engineer's registration and that subscriptions are paid. Foreign engineers need a specific practice permit requested by your firm.

vendors.name: Commercial Registry & Tax Card (via GAFI)
vendors.tagline: GAFI's one-stop company incorporation, online or at 15 Investor Services Centers
vendors.market_position: The General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) runs the one-stop Investor Services Centers where Egyptian companies are incorporated. GAFI says its 15 centers host 67 government entities and that 50,607 companies were incorporated in fiscal year 2025/26. Incorporation gives the business its legal existence; tax registration, sector licences and memberships follow.
pros: GAFI says companies are incorporated in one business day, and sole proprietorships online in two hours
Online incorporation for sole proprietorships, partnerships and LLCs, with fees paid by card and documents signed electronically
After signing, GAFI completes the remaining incorporation steps on the investor's behalf
Investor Services Centers also host the contractors' federation and the New Urban Communities Authority
cons: Incorporation is only the first step: contracting work above EGP 50,000 also needs federation membership under Law 104/1992
GAFI's website does not publish incorporation fees
GAFI's site does not list the documents handed over at incorporation
Permits can take up to 20 business days, per GAFI
vendors.typical_pricing: Official incorporation fees, paid by card during online incorporation; GAFI's website does not publish the amounts.
vendors.eg_specific_note: GAFI's e-incorporation service, launched in September 2023 under Investment Law 72/2017, lets a sole proprietorship, partnership or LLC be set up online: create an account, upload documents, pay fees by card and e-sign the articles and notarization record, after which GAFI completes the remaining steps. Its Investor Services Centers also host the contractors' federation (EFCBC) and NUCA.

vendors.name: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA)
vendors.tagline: Egypt's tax authority: tax registration, VAT, income tax and the mandatory e-invoicing and e-receipt systems
vendors.market_position: The Egyptian Tax Authority administers income tax and VAT and runs the electronic invoicing and electronic receipt systems. Businesses register and update their tax file through its online taxpayer portal. E-invoicing was made mandatory in phases by ETA decisions, and ETA offers an online tool to check whether a taxpayer is covered.
pros: Online taxpayer portal for registration and updating your tax file
Inquiry tools show whether a business must use e-invoicing or e-receipts
Law 6/2025 gives tax incentives and simpler rules to projects with annual turnover up to EGP 20 million
ETA publishes e-invoicing guides, videos and a list of service providers
cons: E-invoices must be electronically signed and sent through integration with ETA's system
VAT and tax procedure laws were amended again in 2025 and 2026, including Law 149/2026
Press reports in October 2025 describe 14% VAT being applied to contracting works, including existing contracts
The VAT registration threshold has been under review since late 2025
vendors.typical_pricing: Official costs are the taxes themselves; the general VAT rate is 14%, still applied in June 2026 amendments per press reports. E-invoicing also needs an electronic signature and a connection to ETA's system, through your own software or one of the service providers ETA lists.
vendors.eg_specific_note: E-invoicing is mandatory for taxpayers named in ETA's phased decisions (phase 5 began on 15 December 2021 and phase 8 ran from September to December 2022); check your status with ETA's inquiry tool. For contractors, ETA lists Ministerial Decision 418/2025 on the tax basis for construction contracts, and October 2025 press reports describe 14% VAT being applied to contracting works.

vendors.name: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI)
vendors.tagline: Egypt's social insurance authority: employer registration and contributions for every insured worker
vendors.market_position: The National Authority for Social Insurance administers Egypt's social insurance and pensions under Law 148 of 2019, in force since 1 January 2020. Employers pay contributions on each insured worker's wage, and workers pay their own share through payroll. The authority runs insurance offices and online services for business owners and insured workers.
pros: Covers workers for old age, disability, death, work injury, sickness and unemployment
Work-injury insurance matters on construction sites, where the employer pays the premium
Online inquiry by insurance number and a service menu for business owners
cons: Employer cost is significant: 12% of wages for old-age, disability and death insurance alone, plus sickness, injury and unemployment shares
Work injuries must be reported to the authority immediately and to the police within 48 hours
High-turnover site crews mean frequent registration changes
The authority's website shows little detail in readable form
vendors.typical_pricing: Statutory contributions under Law 148/2019, paid monthly. Old-age, disability and death insurance is 12% of wages from the employer and 9% from the worker, plus employer shares for work injury (0.5%-1% by risk level, plus 1% for medical care where the worker is not under comprehensive health insurance), sickness (3%, with 1% from the worker) and unemployment (1%).
vendors.eg_specific_note: For contractors, the work-injury rules matter most: under Law 148/2019 the employer pays the injury premium, must notify the authority of each work injury immediately and must report incidents that stop a worker working to the police within 48 hours. Every site worker on the payroll needs to be registered and have contributions paid.

vendors.name: New Urban Communities Authority (NUCA)
vendors.tagline: Planning and building-permit authority for Egypt's new cities, needed per site rather than per company
vendors.market_position: The New Urban Communities Authority is the state body for Egypt's new cities. Under the Unified Building Law 119/2008 (Art. 4) it is the competent planning and organization body for new urban communities, so building permits for sites in new cities such as New Cairo and New Obour come from NUCA rather than a governorate. It is also one of the licensing bodies represented at GAFI's Investors Services Centers.
pros: One authority handles planning and building permits for sites inside the new cities
Represented at GAFI's Investors Services Centers
Issues licensing rule changes and facilitations for new cities, as in its September 2026 decisions
cons: Per project and per site, not a company-wide licence
Only applies inside new urban communities; elsewhere the local administrative body issues permits under Law 119/2008
Building without a permit is prohibited under Law 119/2008 (Art. 39)
Fees and requirements were not readable on NUCA's website
vendors.typical_pricing: Official fees per project for permits and related services; NUCA's website was unreachable and no fee schedule was confirmed.
vendors.eg_specific_note: Check where the site is before planning permits: inside a new city such as New Cairo or New Obour, NUCA is the competent planning and permit body under Law 119/2008 (Art. 4); outside new cities, the local administrative body issues building permits. No building work may start without a permit (Art. 39).
